column12: Judgement on the comparator. Lifyorli is the closest marketed comparator in disease, setting and route: an oral drug approved for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer after 1 to 3 prior lines, the patients MAESTRA 2 enrols (1 to 4). It has a named manufacturer list price, which the brief puts ahead of the CMS convention, and it launched too late for a CMS row. The velzatinib seed annualises a per-pack WAC the same way (Qinlock). Case against, three parts. (1) The WAC is for relacorilant alone, dosed around nab-paclitaxel, which is billed on top; a monotherapy could price above or below it. (2) Elahere, the biomarker-selected incumbent, has only a per-vial WAC ($6,487.15, AbbVie Colorado disclosure, as the sofetabart second reader found): 3 to 4 vials a 21-day cycle is about $19,500 to $26,000, or roughly $340,000 to $450,000 a year, so this anchor sits at or above the class. (3) The engine bills a full year's price to every patient in the treated stock, new starts included. At a constant hazard with a 5.3-month median PFS, mean time on drug is about 7.6 months, so WAC per start is about $315,000, while the engine books 494,054 / 0.7918 = about $624,000 per start at list, roughly twice. The CMS convention absorbs this because spend per beneficiary is already a part-year figure. The nearest CMS figure is Zejula, the oral ovarian PARP inhibitor, at $111,182 per Part D beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Zejula: $224,142,913 over 2,016). It is first-line maintenance, a different setting, and would understate this line by more than this anchor overstates it

column12: Judgement on the biomarker share. MAESTRA 2's cutoff is permissive: at least 75% of tumour cells at IHC 1+ or more (TPS5642). No paper reports prevalence at that cutoff; the phase 1 figure is Incyte's own population but may not use the same definition. The phase 1 was enriched for CCNE1 amplification (56.7%, against about 20% expected in a platinum-resistant trial population per Kim et al., NPJ Precis Oncol 2026, doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01519-6). Re-weighting to 20% amplification gives 0.86 if every amplified tumour overexpresses and 0.94 if 90% do, which brackets 0.922. Case for lower: stricter cutoffs find 51% (azenosertib's clinical cutoff) to 59% (H-score 145 or more) in platinum-resistant trial cohorts (Kim et al. 2026); 42% after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and 61% after a PARP inhibitor at H-score 150 or more (Trecourt et al., Br J Cancer 2026;135:427, doi:10.1038/s41416-026-03440-y); and 22.4% of 3,029 tumours at the OTTA cutoff, mostly at diagnosis (Kang et al., Cancer 2023;129:697, doi:10.1002/cncr.34582). At 0.51 the share would be 0.1064. MAESTRA 2 also requires high-grade serous histology, which the ISPOR counts do not filter. High-grade serous is about 70% of all ovarian cancer (Kim et al.) and more of stage III/IV disease, so this overstates by the non-serous share of advanced platinum-resistant disease, for which no sourced figure was found. Case for higher: MAESTRA 2 admits a fourth prior line (line 5), which lines 2 to 4 leave out. The ISPOR counts are treatment events, so one patient can appear in two lines
